paper.title: Online Learning with an Unknown Fairness Metric

settings.name_in_paper: Known objective case (theta known, Mahalanobis fairness metric unknown)
unmapped: The linear reward parameter theta is known to the learner; only the fairness metric is unknown
Individual (Lipschitz) fairness constraint |pi_i - pi_j| <= d(x_i,x_j) w.r.t. an unknown Mahalanobis distance d(x1,x2)=||A x1 - A x2||
Fairness oracle feedback: after each round the learner observes the set of pairs whose fairness constraint was violated
Two objectives: regret to the best fair policy and number of epsilon-fairness violations
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we consider an easier case of the problem in which the linear objective function $\theta$ is known to the algorithm, and the distance function $d$ is all that is unknown.

settings.name_in_paper: Linear contextual bandits with an unknown Mahalanobis fairness metric (full problem)
unmapped: Individual (Lipschitz) fairness constraint |pi_i - pi_j| <= d(x_i,x_j) w.r.t. an unknown Mahalanobis distance d(x1,x2)=||A x1 - A x2||
Fairness oracle feedback: after each round the learner observes the set of pairs whose fairness constraint was violated
Two objectives: regret to the best fair policy and number of epsilon-fairness violations
settings.definition_quote: An adversary fixes a linear reward function $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $||\theta|| \leq 1$ and a distance function $d$. $\algo$ is given access to the fairness oracle $\cO_d$. In rounds $t = 1$ to $T$: The adversary chooses contexts $x^t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times k}$ with $||x^t_i|| \leq 1$ and gives them to $\algo$. $\algo$ chooses a probability distribution $\pi^t$ over actions, and chooses action $i^t \sim \pi^t$. $\algo$ receives reward $r^t_{i^t}$ and observes feedback $\cO_d(\pi^t)$ from the fairness oracle.

settings.name_in_paper: Generalization to multiple actions (any number of arms per round)
unmapped: Learner may select any subset of the k arms each round (each arm independently with probability p_i in [0,1]), observing rewards of selected arms
Individual (Lipschitz) fairness constraint w.r.t. an unknown Mahalanobis distance with fairness oracle feedback
settings.definition_quote: In our framework, this corresponds to letting the algorithm take as many as $k$ actions on a single day.

source.label: fairloss
source.quote: For any sequence of contexts and any Mahalanobis distance $d(x_1,x_2) = ||Ax_1-Ax_2||_2$: $$\mathbf{FairnessLoss}(\algo_{\textrm{known}-\theta}, T, \epsilon) \leq   O\left(k^2d^2 \log\left(\frac{d \cdot ||A^TA||_F }{\epsilon}\right)\right)$$

results.notes: Bound on epsilon-fairness loss (number of epsilon-unfair pairs summed over rounds), holding with probability 1 per paper's framing.

symbols.eps_alg: accuracy parameter epsilon of the distance estimators

conditions: Mahalanobis distance d(x1,x2)=||A x1 - A x2||_2
tuning: DistanceEstimator copies instantiated with accuracy epsilon^2

source.label: thm:known-regret
source.quote: For any time horizon $T$: $$ \mathbf{Regret}(\algo_{\textrm{known}-\theta},T) \le O\left(k^2d^2 \log\left(\frac{d \cdot ||A^\top A||_F }{\epsilon}\right) + k^3\epsilon T\right) $$ Setting $\epsilon = O(1/(k^3 T))$ yields a regret bound of $O(d^2\log(||A^\top A||_F\cdot dkT))$.

results.notes: Regret to the best fair policy, defined via expected rewards under the played distributions; holds deterministically for every history (theta known). Quantity/probability classification is a judgment call.

source.label: thm:lastregret
source.quote: For any time horizon $T$, with probability $1-\delta$: $$\mathbf{Regret}(\algo_{full},T) \leq O\left(k^2d^2 \log\left(\frac{d \cdot ||A^\top A||_F }{\epsilon}\right) + k^3\epsilon T + d\sqrt{T}\log(\frac{T}{\delta})\right)$$

results.notes: Regret against best fair policy (LP with true rewards and true distances).

conditions: Mahalanobis distance d(x1,x2)=||A x1 - A x2||_2

source.label: thm:lastregret
source.quote: If $\epsilon = 1/{k^3 T}$, this is a regret bound of  $O\left(k^2d^2 \log\left(kdT \cdot ||A^\top A||_F \right) + d\sqrt{T}\log(\frac{T}{\delta})\right)$

results.notes: With this epsilon, fairness loss (Theorem 4) is O(k^2 d^2 log(d k^3 T ||A^TA||_F)).
